description: Fires mainly when the opponent caps my vertical stack in column 5: their stone on row 4 directly above my stones, strongest when I own the three cells below. Same cap in column 3 is weaker. Suppressed when either side has threat cells, by opponent stones in column 2, and on crowded boards (ply above ~20). Also fires weakly in some early openings where the opponent stacks on my stone.
effect: None measurable: forcing it to max or zero changes move probabilities by at most a few points (largest seen: zeroing raised column 3 by 7 points in one position).
notes: 7/8 score calls used (one wasted by running the same program twice). Broad 'opponent caps my stone' rules: F1 0.04-0.17. Adding suppression by threat cells, col-2 opponent stones and ply lifted F1 to 0.397 (P 0.46, R 0.35, AUROC 0.67); final p6 F1 0.394, AUROC 0.695, simulation share 0.10. Minimal pairs confirm the col-5 XXXO cap (e.g. 5,0,5,0,5,5 4.5 vs 5,0,5,0,5,4 0.5) and that the stones must be mine, but the unit is strongly context-modulated and has a diffuse opening component; looks like a mixture. Best F1 just below 0.4, hence low.
